criteria.evidence: TmrApp.kt:125-130 still consumes PendingNavigation for every root but applies it only when startKey.isTopLevelDestination(), so a SignIn start keeps the stack [SignIn]. TmrAppRootTest.pendingKeyAtSignInStart_isDropped (TmrAppRootTest.kt:113) asserts [DefaultSignInNavKey] with a pending Profile key; at bb9e877f the same input produced [SignIn, Profile], so the test fails if the guard is reverted.

Same guard. UploadNavKey is not top level (TopLevelKeys.kt:13 matches only Applications and Profile), so pending keys are dropped. TmrAppRootTest.pendingKeyAtUploadStart_isDropped (:120) asserts [UploadNavKey()].

AppViewModel.kt:37-39: when a resubscribe happens for the same account id, the cached start is emitted again. That Ready equals the held StateFlow value, so nothing recomposes. key(accountId) (TmrApp.kt:95) and the un-keyed rememberNavBackStack keep the stack, so onboarding that completes during the session does not re-root. After process death a new AppViewModel starts with lastHandled == null and reads the start again (:41). observeStartDestination is still awaited with first() over combine(account, onboardingComplete, observeProfile) (ObserveStartDestinationUseCase.kt:17-27), so it waits for the first Room profile emission. rootState_profileReviewedAndOnboardingCompleteAfterStart_doesNotReEmit is unchanged.

Cache scoping: lastHandled is keyed by account id (AppViewModel.kt:38). A sign-out that reaches the UI must first pass the null child, which overwrites lastHandled with (null, SignIn) at :42 before it emits at :43. A later sign-in as the same id or another id therefore misses the cache, reads the start again and refreshes. A cached start cannot be served to a different account id. No timeline was found where user A's start reaches user B. Only flatMapLatest's collector, on the viewModelScope Main.immediate dispatcher, writes lastHandled. The previous child is suspended when it is cancelled, so writes cannot overlap. keepOnly wiring: TmrAppRootTest.accountChange_clearsThePreviousAccountsViewModels (:127) drives TmrApp. The probe ViewModel lives in a per-entry store owned by EntryViewModel inside the account-1 root store. In Nav3 runtime 1.0.0, DecoratedNavEntries.kt calls onPop only for keys missing from the latest back stack, and on a key(accountId) disposal the old stack still holds the key. So only RootViewModelStores.keepOnly (RootViewModelStores.kt:30, called at TmrApp.kt:77-79) clears the probe, and the test fails without that call. Residual stale-frame risk: see finding.

refresh runs only on a cache miss (AppViewModel.kt:44). resubscribeAfterTimeout_sameAccount_doesNotRefreshOrFlashLoading asserts refreshes == 1 after a 6 s unsubscribe, and it would see 2 without the cache. resubscribeAfterTimeout_differentAccount_refreshesAgain asserts 2. Latent, not filed: lastHandled is written before refreshWallet. If the app goes to the background within 5 s of sign-in, WhileSubscribed cancels an in-flight refresh, and the resume hits the cache and never retries. OfflineFirstCreditsRepository.refresh is Unit at this head and on origin/main and revamp/286-network-v2, so nothing is observable today. Re-check when a real wallet refresh lands.

initialValue Loading is unchanged (AppViewModel.kt:51). WhileSubscribed keeps the default replayExpiration, so a resubscribe replays the last Ready and never flashes Loading. The same-account resubscribe test asserts this with expectNoEvents.
Closed by TmrAppRootTest.accountChange_clearsThePreviousAccountsViewModels. Reading confirms the mutation claim (see 272-c5).

The only other initialKeys caller, DebugScenarioActivity.kt:164-168 (debug only), uses the Applications start, so its preview key still applies.
Closed. AppViewModel.kt:50 now uses SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000), as Constitution II.2 requires. The c6 exactly-once property is kept by the per-account lastHandled cache.

TmrApp.kt:74 entryProvider only changes how a key renders (TmrApp.kt:133-141). The start key, the key(accountId) re-root, keepOnly and the pending-key guard all run before it and do not depend on it, so it cannot bypass the gate. The only production caller, MainActivity.kt:32, does not pass it.

findings.rule: 272-c5 (sign-out or session expiry re-roots to Sign in); review checklist 4 (stale or cached state). This is the cost of complying with Constitution II.2.
findings.trigger: User A starts a long backend request, for example tailoring, then sends the app to the background for more than 5 s, which stops the upstream. The request comes back 401 or account-gone, and SessionExpiryHandler.onSessionExpired (SessionExpiryHandler.kt:34-56, ApplicationScope) signs A out while nothing collects. On return, collectAsStateWithLifecycle (MainActivity.kt:30) gets the replayed Ready(start, A). TmrApp keeps A's root and stack, which are composed and interactive, until the restarted upstream finishes its DataStore read and the cache-miss observeStartDestination().first() Room read (AppViewModel.kt:41) and emits Ready(SignIn, null). With the previous Eagerly, the StateFlow already held Ready(SignIn, null), and the first resumed frame showed Sign in. resubscribeAfterTimeout_differentAccount_refreshesAgain asserts this replay of the stale account. The window is a few frames and shows the same person's last screen, so there is no cross-user leak.
findings.title: After a background sign-out (>5 s stopped), the resumed UI briefly re-renders the signed-out account's root before the restarted upstream emits Sign in
findings.proof: Turbine: send account A, collect and cancel, advanceTimeBy(6_000), sendAccount(null), then resubscribe. The first item is Ready(Upload, A), not Ready(SignIn, null). Suggested disposition: record it as an accepted trade-off of II.2 in the PR Decisions. A code fix is optional, for example letting TmrApp drop the root when sessionRepository reports no account.
